title: The Fable 5 Export Controls Harm US Cyber Defense
description: Kate Moussouris confirms that the 'jailbreak' that led to Claude Fable 5 being banned under export controls was simply asking the model to 'fix this code' with known CVEs. This is absurd because coding models fixing bugs is crucial for defensive security - finding, fixing, and testing patches is exactly what defenders need AI to do. Non-technical decision-makers are ready to ban models that help secure code.
author: Simon Willison (citing Kate Moussouris)

title: Cloudflare CAPTCHA optimization with Claude Code
description: Used Claude Code to optimize Cloudflare CAPTCHA rules - now only triggers for search URLs containing at least one ampersand, allowing simple ?q=term searches to work without challenge. Also tried Cloudflare MCP with Claude Code but had to switch to Cloudflare API directly.
author: Simon Willison

title: datasette-agent 0.3a0 with user approval for write operations
description: New execute_write_sql tool requests user approval before writing to database, taking user permissions into account. Enhanced datasette agent chat terminal mode supports approvals, with new --root, --yes, and --unsafe options. Can now use 'datasette agent chat content.db -m gpt-5.5 --unsafe' to directly modify databases through natural language prompts.
author: Simon Willison

title: Personality clashes behind Anthropic's model suspension
description: Behind-the-scenes reporting on US government export control of Mythos/Fable models. Anthropic's red team members (Logan Graham, Dave Orr, Nicholas Carlini) meeting with Commerce Department. Sources suggest the situation may come down to making everyone 'feel safe, secure and happy' rather than technical fixes.
author: Simon Willison (citing Axios reporting)

title: Why AI hasn't replaced software engineers, and won't
description: Arvind Narayanan and Sayash Kappor analyze AI job displacement through the lens of software engineering. Data shows no AI-related mass layoffs (160 WARN Act filings, zero checked AI box). Real bottlenecks aren't typing code but: (1) deciding and specifying what to build, (2) verifying and being accountable for deliveries, (3) deep human understanding of codebase, business, and environment.
author: Simon Willison (citing Arvind Narayanan and Sayash Kappor)

title: Mapping SQLite result columns back to their source table.column
description: Research project to programmatically identify which table.column each result column came from in arbitrary SQL queries. Used Claude Code (Opus 4.8) to explore multiple solutions: apsw, ctypes accessing sqlite3_column_table_name(), and clever interrogation of EXPLAIN output. Enables rendering Datasette queries with additional metadata.
author: Simon Willison

title: US government directive suspends Fable 5 and Mythos 5 access
description: Anthropic received export control directive to suspend all access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 by any foreign national due to alleged jailbreak. Government cited 'a method of bypassing' but Anthropic's review found it's just asking models to 'read a specific codebase and fix any software flaws' - capabilities widely available in other models like GPT-5.5. Access cut off at 6:59pm Pacific on June 12.
author: Simon Willison (citing Anthropic statement)

title: OpenAI WebRTC Audio Session with document context
description: Enhanced OpenAI WebRTC audio tool to use GPT-Realtime-2 model (GPT-5-class reasoning) and support pasting document context for audio conversations. Enables conversational exploration of documents in browser with voice model.
author: Simon Willison

title: Claude Fable is relentlessly proactive
description: After two days with Claude Fable 5, describes it as 'relentlessly proactive' - knows a whole lot of tricks and deploys pretty much any of them to reach goals. Includes detailed examples of Fable's aggressive problem-solving approach.
author: Simon Willison

title: Datasette 1.0a33 with JSON extras in the API
description: Significant step toward Datasette 1.0, extending ?_extra= pattern to queries and rows. Had Claude Fable 5 (for planning) and GPT-5.5 xhigh in Codex Desktop (for implementation) build a custom extras API explorer. Demonstrates how API explorer tools are almost free to build with current AI models.
author: Simon Willison

title: Anthropic walks back invisible frontier LLM development safeguards
description: Wired scoop: Anthropic changing Fable 5 safeguards for frontier LLM development to make them visible. Previously, Fable would silently limit effectiveness for requests targeting frontier LLM development (pretraining pipelines, distributed training, ML accelerator design) through prompt modification, steering vectors, or PEFT - affecting ~0.03% of traffic. @ClaudeDeets announced flagged requests will visibly fall back to Opus 4.8.
author: Simon Willison (citing Wired and Anthropic)

title: Datasette Agent 0.2a0 with user questions
description: Tools can now ask user questions mid-execution using context.ask_user() for yes/no, multiple-choice, or free-text questions. Conversations suspend while questions are unanswered, persisting across server restarts. Built-in save_query tool saves SQL as Datasette stored queries with human approval.
author: Simon Willison

title: DuckDB untrusted SQL security research
description: Investigation into whether DuckDB can run untrusted SQL as safely as Datasette runs SQLite. Found DuckDB can be sandboxed to match SQLite safety but requires more than basic read_only=True. Datasette uses engine-level read-only and opcode-based time limits.
author: Simon Willison

title: DiffusionGemma open weight model
description: Google's DiffusionGemma research returned as Apache 2 licensed open weight model (google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it). NVIDIA hosting free on NIM cloud API. Generated image took 4.4s for 2,409 tokens (500+ tokens/second). Previously experimental Gemini Diffusion model from May 2025.
author: Simon Willison

title: If Claude Fable stops helping you, you'll never know
description: Analysis of Anthropic's invisible safeguards for frontier LLM development in Fable 5/Mythos 5. Models silently limit effectiveness for requests targeting ML infrastructure through prompt modification, steering vectors, or PEFT - affecting ~0.03% of traffic. First time Anthropic announced silent interventions. Jeremy Howard notes this creates power imbalance as Anthropic can use Fable for frontier AI research while preventing others from doing so.
author: Simon Willison (citing Jeremy Howard)
